item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 122307
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Mon Oct 12 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Simon, located within a hundred miles west of Cabo Corrientes,
Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico (EP93):
Showers and thunderstorms are beginning to show signs of
organization in association with a broad area of low pressure
located several hundred miles south-southwest of the coast of
Guatemala. This system is gradually becoming better defined, and
environmental conditions are forecast to be conducive for further
development. A tropical depression or tropical storm is expected to
form well south of southern Mexico later tonight or tomorrow while
the system moves generally west-northwestward at around 10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...near 100 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...near 100 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Simon Public Advisory Number 23
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Mon Oct 12 2026 
000
WTPZ35 KNHC 130253
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Simon Advisory Number  23
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
800 PM MST Mon Oct 12 2026
 
...SIMON MOVING SLOWLY TO THE WEST-NORTHWEST...
...FLOODING RAINS TO CONTINUE ALONG THE COAST OF WEST-CENTRAL
MEXICO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM MST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.4N 107.0W
ABOUT 85 MI...135 KM W OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
ABOUT 195 MI...315 KM S OF MAZATLAN MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...100 MPH...155 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 3 MPH...6 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...969 MB...28.62 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The government of Mexico has replaced the Hurricane Watch from Cabo
Corrientes to Escuinapa with a Tropical Storm Watch.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* North of Esuinapa to Bahia Tempehuaya
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Cabo Corrientes to Escuinapa
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area within 48 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere in west-central Mexico should continue to
monitor as changes to watches and warnings are possible later today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM MST (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Simon was located
near latitude 20.4 North, longitude 107.0 West. Simon is moving
toward the west-northwest near 3 mph (6 km/h). A turn to the 
northwest is expected to occur later tonight. Simon is expected to 
continue on a slow, northwestward motion over the next couple of 
days, followed by a turn to the north shortly thereafter. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 100 mph (155 km/h) with higher
gusts. Weakening is forecast over the next day or so, but Simon
could re-intensify some by Wednesday and is forecast to remain a
hurricane through midweek.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 10 miles (20 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles
(75 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 969 mb (28.62 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are likely to occur in Las Islas Marias
beginning on Tuesday. Hurricane conditions are possible
within the hurricane watch area on Wednesday, with tropical storm
conditions possible by Tuesday night. Tropical storm conditions are
possible within the tropical storm watch area on Tuesday and
Wednesday.
 
RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce rainfall totals of 5 to 10
inches across coastal west-central Mexico with isolated maximum
amounts of 15 inches over the state of Sinaloa by Thursday.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: A dangerous storm surge is possible along the immediate
coast near Las Islas Marias. Near the coast, the surge will be
accompanied by large and destructive waves.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 1100 PM MST.
Next complete advisory at 200 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 23
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Mon Oct 12 2026 
584 
WTPZ45 KNHC 130255
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number  23
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
800 PM MST Mon Oct 12 2026
 
Simon's convection has degraded quite a bit since the last advisory.
Given how much of this weakening has been concentrated across the
eastern half of the storm, it is possible that Simon has been
ingesting dry, high terrain air into its center. Regardless of the
physical mechanism, however, both subjective and objective Dvorak
intensity estimates have picked up on this weakening trend, as the
TAFB Dvorak classification rates Simon at 5.0/90 kt and UW-CIMSS
estimates range from 51 to 72 kt. As a result of these data, Simon's
initial intensity has been lowered to 85 kt.
 
The storm motion remains very slow at 305/3 kt. Simon is riding the
western flank of a high pressure ridge centered over the
southeastern US, with high pressure building to the storm's west as
well in the wake of a deep trough currently enveloping the
Intermountain West. Simon is battling a multitude of features
influencing its motion as a result, and track guidance continues to
exhibit a wide spread of solutions. Thus, confidence in the track
forecast remains low. The global models, however, do seem to agree
that the high anchored over the southeastern US will remain for at
least the next 48 hours, so the current forecast thinking is that
Simon will not make a turn toward land in the meantime. What becomes
of that high once the aforementioned trough moves eastward across
the US is what will ultimately determine Simon's path.
 
Looking at the global models, the GFS depicts the trough doing
little to erode the southeastern high, leaving Simon to become
caught in a col as it is wedged between two high pressure systems,
thus causing it to become nearly stationary over the next couple of
days. The ECMWF, however, seems to suggest that the trough will dig
deep enough to cause a turn to the northeast toward land over the
next 48 hours. More skilled guidance like the HCCA and GDMI,
however, seem to favor a due northwest track, likely stemming from
the southeastern US high remaining fixed in place and the high to
the west not building enough to affect Simon's motion. The latest
NHC track forecast favors this solution, while still depicting a
turn to the northeast after a couple of days should this Pacific
high strengthen enough to nudge Simon off its current trajectory.
 
Should Simon continue to move northwestward, as is currently
forecast, gradual re-strengthening should follow. The environment
just off the coast of west-central Mexico continues to be defined by
low vertical wind shear, anomalously warm SSTs, and ample mid-level
moisture. Should the storm become nearly stationary as some models
suggest, however, re-intensification could be inhibited by Simon
churning up cooler waters from deep below the sea surface. It should
be noted that the current consensus across the guidance does not
favor a period of rapid intensification, so the latest NHC intensity
forecast continues to reflect a more gradual upward trend in
strength, before dropping off sharply once Simon makes its
forecasted approach to land. With confidence lacking in the track
forecast, however, Simon's intensity forecast confidence is only low
to moderate.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Hurricane conditions are likely on Las Islas Marias over the
next day or so, where a Hurricane Warning remains in effect.
 
2. Simon could approach the coast of western Mexico later this week,
where hurricane conditions are possible.
 
3. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of
west-central Mexico over the next few days. This rainfall will
produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas
of steep terrain.
 
4. Large swells will affect portions of the southwestern and
west-central coasts of Mexico over the next several days. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
